elements.quote: The inclusion criteria, based on the PICO framework, are as follows: ① Population: Patients with post-stroke depression (PSD) meeting the diagnostic criteria. ② Intervention: The experimental group includes TCE such as Tai Chi, Baduanjin, Yijinjing, and Wuqinxi, while the control group receives standard care, health education, or routine treatment. ③ Outcome: ... ④ Study Design: Only randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included.
elements.reason: Full PICO-based eligibility criteria including population, intervention/comparator, outcomes, and study design are explicitly specified, though setting and follow-up requirements are not detailed.

elements.quote: First, although both Chinese and English literature were screened, all included studies were in Chinese, likely because exercises such as Tai Chi and Qigong are unique to China.
elements.reason: Language restrictions are implied (Chinese and English screened) in the Limitations, but dissemination year and publication status criteria are only partially inferable from exclusion criteria (e.g., dissertations, conference proceedings excluded); no explicit report-characteristics eligibility criteria (year, language, status) are stated in the methods.

elements.quote: ① Dissertations, conference proceedings, studies without full text access, or those with missing data. ... ④ Studies with outcome measures not aligned with the objectives of this research.
elements.reason: Exclusion criteria distinguish studies with missing data/unavailable full text (results not reported/accessible) from studies whose outcome measures do not align with review objectives (outcomes not measured).

elements.quote: The experimental group includes TCE such as Tai Chi, Baduanjin, Yijinjing, and Wuqinxi, while the control group receives standard care, health education, or routine treatment.
elements.reason: The synthesis groups (TCE intervention vs standard care/health education/routine treatment control) are defined within the PICO criteria and linked to the review objective of evaluating TCE effects on PSD; subgroup analysis is mentioned but subgroup groupings are not detailed, so this is at the lower bound of PRESENT.

elements.quote: Thus, the quest for an effective, safe, and easily implementable non-pharmacological treatment becomes imperative.
elements.reason: A general rationale for focusing on TCE as a non-pharmacological intervention is provided in the background, but explicit rationales for specific restrictions such as excluding patients with comorbid malignancies or severe hepatic/renal dysfunction are not given.
